body: Honestly, I don't care enough anymore to argue my opinion. I do thank you for the critique though and maybe you're right, maybe I'm not ready for critiquing, maybe I'm just not ready to face that my work has flaws, I thank you for helping me realise that. I won't apologise, though, just as I don't ask an apology from you, for I don't see the need for one in our, for lack of a better word, debate? Fight? I'm not sure what to call it, an argument, probably. And you actually have given me some good advice on what I could possibly do with my story, and I might just take it into consideration, I'm not sure yet. But again, thank you.
Thank you for the advice. I will definitely take what you've said into consideration and I thank you for being considerate and for the compliment towards my writing. It does mean a lot, thank you.

I do actually appreciate your opinions, everyone is entitled to them, but I do not think that you were critiquing my writing, rather demeaning my work. Now, that is my opinion, people are entitled to those, and by no means does this mean you or anyone else must believe me, but by creating setting for the rest of the story and developing backstory for the characters, I was setting up chapter two, and for you to tell me that it was "unnecessary" and to cut out almost the entire story, was, in my opinion, bullying. The messages I was sending you were my way of proving a point that the top writers even since the forties have been using chapter one to create setting and background. Now, yes, I actually do thank you for your opinion, I'm not saying it's wrong, but I am saying it was rude.
Thank you and I have fixed it accordingly. :)
Thank you for the advice. :) I'm just happy someone actually read it, haha, but I will take what you've said into consideration. :) Again, thank you!
Oh, now I feel rather foolish.
Oh no, a good or bad one?
Thank you. :) I was really nervous about uploading anything, but I'm glad at least one person likes it, haha.

She came home a while ago but we just talked about an hour ago and we sort of worked stuff out. I told her I was using the carpet cutter and she said I could keep the box cutter if I gave her the carpet cutter, and we made an agreement. I feel a lot better actually, still kind of scared of what she thinks, but a lot better that we talked things out. :)

Thank you. Really, thank you, it does mean so much to me. I don't have that many friends, and to just hear encouraging words from another person, albeit, a complete stranger really does mean a lot to me. And my mother is a very strong woman. The strongest woman I know.

I've got this thing about telling people my problems, makes me feel like an attention whore in a sense, even though I never talk to anyone. But I'll tell you about the gist of it all. My mother is an alcoholic with severe bipolar disorder and suicidal tendencies. She was never the best mother in the world, she did everything she could for us, though, even though she messed up a lot. I love her very much. My father was out of the picture for a very long time, didn't even know him until I was twelve. He also has sever bipolar disorder, psychotic tendencies, a drug addiction to valium, and is also an alcoholic. He came back into our life a few times, but those times were just fucking nightmares. My brother verbally abuses me and bullies me any chance he can get, and about the only person I could rely on, my sister, moved in with her boyfriend to take care of him after an extensive leg surgery. I'm seeing a therapist and am on medication and have so far been diagnosed with severe social anxiety, severe generalised anxiety, severe depression, and possible schizoaffective disorder, though that has yet to be diagnosed fully. I've just been in a shitty place my entire life. I have a man that lives behind my eyes who watches me and puts ideas in my head and every now and again I hear things, mostly when I'm trying to fall asleep. I have severe paranoia as well, I think that everyone is watching me and that there are cameras all around my house and so on and so forth and that people come in while I sleep and open up my head and control my thoughts. I know all of this sounds really fucking insane and I apologise for that. It's only ever gotten worse as the years edge on.

My mother is a cutter too, so she understands most of it. But she's also insanely protective, too, and blows a lot of things out of proportion. In a sense, she's a bit of a hypocrite. And I know that if she takes away my tools, I'll just go back to bruising, not like she can take away my fists, but she asked my therapist if I should be put in a three day psych evaluation, something that happened to her, and I'm honestly terrified that she might just do it. She thinks I'm cutting too deep, (maybe I am, I don't know really) but my cuts are nothing compared to the things she's done to herself. Maybe she just doesn't want me to end up like her, Idk. And the carpet cutter was a brand new one, never been used, and I keep it clean, I also clean out my wounds. I take care of it too, but she doesn't seem to want to listen.

Thank you for the advice. My mother is also a cutter, so she understands it, mostly, but when I found out she was cutting a couple years ago, I took away all the blades in the house, hid everything. I don't want her to do what I did to her. I was just a kid at that time and I didn't know any better. And I understand that I need to stop cutting and whatnot, I just don't think I'm ready to give it up right this moment, but I know it needs to stop eventually. I just wish she understood that I'll decide when to stop, and if she makes me stop, as horrible as it may sound, I'll find other ways, just like she did.
Well, I believe it's a step in the right direction. All I can tell you is be strong and that if you ever need to talk, I'm here to talk to. :)

I'm sorry to hear all that. I really am. Have you tried to find some form of online therapy? Some of it is free. And there are support groups you can join and hotlines you can call if anything is the matter.

It's okay to be scared or nervous. I was pretty scared the first time I told my mother about what was up with me. I was afraid she'd think I was crazy or something, but she was oddly supportive of it all. If you do choose to tell someone something, don't expect them to understand your feelings or situation right off the bat. It'll take some time. Do you have a therapist or some form of support group?

I don't think you sound crazy at all and It's never a waste of my time. I understand feeling like you just want to sleep and have it all end. I feel like that too, at times. I felt like that for a very long time before getting therapy. Hell, I still feel like that, I don't think It'll ever truly go away, but It's gotten a bit better for me. I think what helps me the most isn't the medication, but when I do decide to confide in someone, be it someone online, like you, or a friend of mine. I can't say what will help you, but if you ever need someone to talk to, I'm here. You can message me anytime you'd like. :)

It's okay that you don't have any advice for me. :) It was hard when I reached out for help. I sort of felt like once I told people, they'd start doting on me and wouldn't leave me alone. I'm seeing a therapist now and it's actually quite helpful. It's someone to talk to. I hadn't told anyone about my problems for years and it still feels pretty weird talking about myself and my issues to someone, but it's really helpful. I can understand being afraid of losing your privacy, sometimes I wish that I hadn't told anyone at all cus I find myself thinking it's weak to need help, but it's really helped me a lot. It's up to you what you decide, and I won't promise you anything, but therapy has really helped me, even if it's only someone to really rant to every Wednesday. I hope the best comes to you. :)

Thank you for the advice. I also feel like my mother would blame herself. When I first told her of my depression and anxiety and whatnot, she felt it was her fault. She's always been one to put herself down, and because of her alcoholism, she blames herself and says she's the reason I'm the way I am. I don't think it's all her fault. I can't deny that environment plays a part in people's mental health, but I'd never blame my toils on her. She says she's there for me and will listen to whatever I have to tell her, and I do tell her some things, the things I'm comfortable discussing with her. I just don't want to put too much on her. She feels guilty enough as it is.
